title: Simple programs yield a straightforward explanation of thermodynamic behavior

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Simple programs yield a straightforward explanation of thermodynamic behavior

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The long-standing difficulty in understanding how thermodynamic behavior, including the Second Law of Thermodynamics, arises in physics can be resolved by a straightforward explanation drawn from the behavior of simple programs.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. 1: The Foundations for a New Kind of Science

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: For more than a century, for example, there has been confusion about how thermodynamic behavior arises in physics. Yet from my discoveries about simple programs I have developed a quite straightforward explanation.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 1, “The Foundations for a New Kind of Science”; section “An Outline of Basic Ideas” (from p. 1), p. 4. Scope: thermodynamics and statistical mechanics, specifically the basis of entropy increase

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch01-06: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.59

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Thermodynamic data and simulations are abundant, and specific derived predictions can be tested. The broad claim of resolving the conceptual basis of the Second Law is not discriminated merely by reproducing familiar macroscopic behavior.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Formalize the proposed simple-program account of entropy increase and derive predictions for relaxation, recurrence, and entropy production in specified systems. Compare these against existing statistical-mechanics simulations and experimental time series and against standard rival accounts.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Agreement with entropy increase may not distinguish this account from standard statistical mechanics.

Straightforward explanation is not itself a measurable outcome.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.8
operationalizability: 0.45
analysis feasibility: 0.55
discriminating power: 0.35
data adequacy: 0.75

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Thermodynamic tables and reversible-automaton simulations both exist, so the computational illustration and the numerical facts of thermodynamics can be put side by side. They do not isolate this explanation from the Boltzmann and ergodic accounts, which predict the same increase of entropy. The claim that the program picture resolves the foundational difficulty therefore stays only partly testable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Derive a second-law statement from an explicit simple-program model, then compare its entropy production and equilibrium statistics with laboratory thermodynamic data and with the Boltzmann account. Confirmation requires a distinguishing prediction that the data favor; a simulation that merely increases a coarse-grained entropy does not.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Resolving a conceptual difficulty is not a dataset outcome.

Coarse-graining choices can manufacture or remove an entropy increase.

Entropy increase in a typical reversible system is also predicted by ordinary statistical mechanics.
